title: Made a spritesheet slicer to get multiple assets out of one image
author: Chologism
selftext:
Finally added the last missing piece of my bulk asset workflow:

Being able to automatically slice animations into individual spritesheets.

Why?

1. AI image gen gives you better style consistency when assets share one canvas.   
2. It reduces the cost dramatically, the example is 49 characters with one nano banana 2 call.

The problems:

The output is one big sheet. Slicing it up by hand in Photoshop is a chore. Worse for animations, since you have to keep frame alignment across the whole strip.

AI never gives you perfect spacing. Stuff bleeds into neighboring tiles (never a perfect rectangle space around it). 

So I built a slicer into my app. For animations it crops the same region across every frame, so you get back a proper animated sprite.

To solve the bleending issue, the slicer detects connected pixel islands inside each rectangle and keeps only the main one. 

**Note about the clip:** The monsters are by no means super quality output. I was just pushing how much you can cram into one generation. Zero manual cleanup either, a bit of touchup would go a long way.

replies.author: Chologism
replies.body:
Yes, this is a platform I'm developing specifically for AI game art generation

It started out as a CLI tool I built for myself, because I got tired of writing the same prompt instructions to nano banana for every asset but has now grown into a full app

I wrote more about the slicer here:  
[https://www.spritecook.ai/blog/slice-sprite-sheets-and-animations](https://www.spritecook.ai/blog/slice-sprite-sheets-and-animations)

comments.body: Looks really good honestly. Any way to try it out with my own reference pixel art? I'm missing these steps in my current workflow. Looking for a good alternative.

replies.author: Chologism
replies.body:
Yep, only right now it's a bit tricky to use uploaded images directly in the slicer, that's something that I have to make easier..

You would have to upload your image in the editor, and save as new asset  
[https://app.spritecook.ai/editor](https://app.spritecook.ai/editor)

and then open it in the slicer tool  
[https://www.spritecook.ai/blog/slice-sprite-sheets-and-animations](https://www.spritecook.ai/blog/slice-sprite-sheets-and-animations)

replies.author: Chologism
replies.body:
Yep, you can prompt it for anything, supports both pixel art and detailed animations  
[https://www.spritecook.ai/blog/animate-custom-sprites](https://www.spritecook.ai/blog/animate-custom-sprites)

For characters I made a separate flow to make make it easier to get consistant results:  
[https://www.spritecook.ai/blog/character-creator-flow](https://www.spritecook.ai/blog/character-creator-flow)

comments.author: Juzzaman
comments.body:
Are you working on adding to animations? I have a workflow I can't find a solution to anywhere.

I'm making a game where I have a few base sprites a tons of equipment. I need to be able to get a few base animations, idle, walk, attack, get hit, death and then I need to apply chainmail, sword, shields etc, to it and get back the added animation as a separate animation spritesheet. On it's own it'd look like a floating sword, but together I can add/remove tons of animation variations.

replies.body: I noticed some export artifacts appear to be generated client-side before the subscription gate is checked. If paid access is meant to control exports, you may want to verify that entitlement checks happen server-side before generating or returning downloadable assets, not only before rendering download buttons in the UI.

replies.body: It's always an ad on here. It's also funny how all these vibe coded AI online apps think they are worthy of being a subscription service. Even Adobe gets a ton of flak for subscriptions because most people hate them.

replies.author: monsterfurby
replies.body:
Yeah... you'd think that tooling being so easy now would lead to people being *more* inclined to share their progress and the tools they make. I've made a few tools for colleagues and people in various communities just because I thought it would be fun and also help someone out. 

But instead we get people who think they're the next Steve Jobs because they made a mildly useful wrapper/frontend. It's still probably cool, but not everything has to be a damn product.

replies.author: Trashy_io
replies.body: Nice! is there an easy way to edit them as well? as thats what I am trying to solve with my workflow as well as the consistency angle. I take a similar approach but less assets per batch, Ive found the LLM will start to hallucinate when you asked for too much at once. as well as not trying one shot but more like 3-5 prompt editing style. I think if you had an option for the amount of assets per gen and a inline lite editor if you don't have one already would make it an all in one hub and help with quality per output as well! Thats my plan with my work flow!
